title: Top 10 Global Fabless IC Design Houses Post 73% YoY Revenue Growth in 2Q26 Says TrendForce
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

The world’s 10 largest fabless chip designers generated more than $141.45 billion in revenue during the second quarter of 2026, a 73% increase from a year earlier, according to TrendForce. The surge underscores how artificial intelligence spending is reshaping the semiconductor hierarchy, lifting suppliers of GPUs, CPUs, custom accelerators and high-speed networking while leaving smartphone-focused vendors under pressure.

Nvidia remained the dominant player. Its quarterly revenue climbed 99% year over year to nearly $91.16 billion, equal to 64% of the top 10’s combined sales. Demand broadened beyond hyperscale cloud providers to include NeoCloud operators, sovereign AI projects and enterprises. Broadcom held second place as revenue jumped 112% to more than $18.89 billion, supported by custom AI silicon and networking products.

AMD advanced to third with revenue above $11.53 billion. TrendForce linked the move to the growing importance of CPUs in agentic AI systems, alongside continued share gains in x86 servers. Qualcomm slipped to fourth, earning more than $8.5 billion as smartphone weakness and a smaller share of modems in Apple’s newest iPhone offset continued automotive growth. MediaTek placed fifth with about $4.81 billion, while Marvell ranked sixth at $2.63 billion as demand rose for 800G and 1.6T interconnect products.

The remaining positions went to Realtek, Monolithic Power Systems, Novatek and OmniVision, which are pursuing growth in servers, AI power management, edge AI and optical communications.

Bottom line: The results show that the AI boom is expanding beyond graphics processors. Value is shifting toward an entire compute stack spanning CPUs, custom accelerators, networking, power management and optical links. AMD’s rise signals a more diversified market, but Nvidia’s 64% share also reveals extreme concentration. For investors and supply-chain companies, the clearest opportunities increasingly sit with vendors tied to data-center infrastructure, while dependence on mature smartphone and PC markets remains a drag.

TrendForce — original report, September 11, 2026 — Primary source for the rankings, revenue figures and company analysis.
